analysis.title: Macro Volatility Digest
key_insights: Implied volatilities rose across asset classes last week as oil gained on geopolitical tensions and investors pulled back from Tech and AI stocks ahead of key earnings.
Oil volatility jumped the most: OVX up over 9 pts week on week to 60% (70th percentile over the past year), with Brent ending the week near a 1-year high.
Credit volatility kept climbing: VIXIG up another 3 pts to a 6-month high of 35 (90th percentile), more than double IG credit realized volatility, as AI debt concerns escalate.

Interest rate volatility gained modestly ahead of this week's FOMC meeting. The Fed is widely expected to hold (~90% implied probability per OIS), and focus is on hawkish dissents and press conference signals on the rate path for December and 2027.
SPX options imply a one-day move of ~1.3% for Wednesday's Fed meeting, the same as for next week's US mid-term elections.
FX is the only asset class where implied volatility is still trading significantly below average.
The VIX ended the week mostly unchanged at 19.5%, which masked sector rotation under the surface (Comm Svc down 6.2% vs Energy up 1.6%).
Implied stock dispersion (DSPX) rose to 37% (63rd percentile) entering a key week of mega-cap Tech earnings.
The QQQ-SPX 1M implied vol spread widened to ~10%, over 2 standard deviations above its long-term average and just below the July extremes, reflecting concern over the AI trade.

Expanded trading hours for 24 of the most actively traded single stock options went live last week. Over 180k contracts traded in the first week, with the 7:30-9:25am morning session making up nearly 93% of the flow. Cboe expects liquidity to grow as more brokers enable extended hours.
SPX 1M skew (25-delta ratio) ended the week in the 69th percentile (vs 90th a week ago) as upside call chasing in the early rebound gave way to renewed hedging after the end-of-week sell-off.
Demand for tail risk protection, measured by SPX downside convexity (10D vs 25D ratio), stayed in the 99th percentile, though off the extremes of a week ago.
Retail positioning in Tech turned more cautious ahead of earnings: call demand in mega-cap Tech fell to a 6-month low while put demand rose to a 1-year high.
earnings_insights: Mega-cap Tech earnings are due this week, and the QQQ-SPX implied vol spread (~10%) shows a rising volatility premium for Tech earnings risk. No company-level EPS or revenue figures are given.
